reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 108:10-13 = MT 108:11-14; all four in-field pairings reproduce under ps_lib.web_to_mt ((108,11), (108,12), (108,13), (108,14)). Every curly-quoted WEB string verifies verbatim (check_web_quotes.py GREEN across the cluster's 38 quotes), check_refs_mirror.py is clean for this row, and confidence high is calibrated for a span with one forced edge and one discourse-marked edge. Two observations, neither rising to a defect. First, check_universals.py flags two absence phrases here, 'carries no discourse marker separating it from the' and 'with no intervening topic marker'; both are reading claims rather than countable objects, no sweep could settle them, and nothing in the bytes contradicts either. Second, this row is the only 1 of the cluster's 8 rows with no original-language evidence at all -- and a byte-tier anchor was available: web:Ps.108.13 = oshb:Ps.108.14 is byte-identical to web:Ps.60.12 = oshb:Ps.60.14 (equality test True), the only byte-equal pair in the entire 108/60 tail (108:8 and 108:13 match only at skeleton tier; 108:9, 108:10, 108:11 and 108:12 differ in consonants). challenges.claim: The 'fatherless-root spelling' sweep names one object but its digits belong to a truncated consonantal substring that is not a spelling; neither attested spelling in the span yields 2-of-4, and the figure silently omits half the lexeme's book-wide attestation.

Read as the root count the sentence advertises, it is short by half: because final-letter allography is preserved exactly in this extract, the final-mem spelling of the same lexeme sweeps to 4 further verses (oshb:Ps.10.14, oshb:Ps.10.18, oshb:Ps.82.3, oshb:Ps.146.9), putting the fatherless lexeme in 8 verses book-wide, not 4. Confidence medium is calibrated. Two observations short of defects. First, device_notes delimits the clothing image as web:Ps.109.17-Ps.109.19, but the clothing verb of oshb:Ps.109.18 recurs outside that range at oshb:Ps.109.29 (יִלְבְּשׁ֣וּ; that skeleton = 2 verses inside Ps 109, oshb:Ps.109.18 and oshb:Ps.109.29), alongside וְיַעֲט֖וּ answering יַעְטֶ֑ה at oshb:Ps.109.19 -- the delimitation survives only on a narrow reading of clothing-as-curse against 109:29's clothing-as-shame, which the note does not say. Neither touches the span, the warrant, or the row's own counts.

Span WEB 109:21-27 = MT 109:21-27 (identity). All four Hebrew runs collate at BYTE tier at their stated refs, including the divine-name sequence וְאַתָּ֤ה יְה֘וִ֤ה אֲדֹנָ֗י עֲֽשֵׂה at oshb:Ps.109.21, and pmarks_Ps.json records no ketiv/qere anywhere in Ps 109, so no disclosure is owed on it. The 20|21 seam is in fact well warranted -- on grounds the row states in passing rather than the one it names: the fronted וְאַתָּ֤ה against the demonstrative verdict-label opening oshb:Ps.109.20, and the switch from a 3ms curse-object to a 1cs petitioner. challenges.claim: The row's stated driver -- that direct second-person address to God is absent from oshb:Ps.109.1-Ps.109.20 -- is falsified by the psalm's own first verse.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.109.1 = לַ֭מְנַצֵּחַ לְדָוִ֣ד מִזְמ֑וֹר אֱלֹהֵ֥י תְ֝הִלָּתִ֗י אַֽל תֶּחֱרַֽשׁ . That verse sits inside the very range the claim excludes. A second instance stands inside the stretch the row calls a third-person curse register: oshb:Ps.109.6 opens on הַפְקֵ֣ד, a 2ms imperative under the non-quoted reading of 109:6-19 that this psalm's rows take as the main line, rendered “Set a wicked man over him.” (web:Ps.109.6). The claim is made twice: hedged in rationale as 'absent from web:Ps.109.1-Ps.109.20's third-person report/curse register', and unhedged in observed_substrate_signals as 'a direct second-person address to God absent from oshb:Ps.109.1-Ps.109.20'. observed_substrate_signals is the field a downstream reader treats as the substrate fact, and as written it is false. What the bytes do support is that oshb:Ps.109.21 opens the first SUSTAINED stretch of second-person address -- 7 consecutive verses of it, oshb:Ps.109.21 to oshb:Ps.109.27 -- which is a different and defensible warrant.

challenges.evidence: The 109:6 token skeleton sweeps to 8 verses (web:Ps.20.6 = oshb:Ps.20.7, oshb:Ps.78.54, web:Ps.89.25 = oshb:Ps.89.26, oshb:Ps.90.9, oshb:Ps.90.12, oshb:Ps.90.14, oshb:Ps.98.1, oshb:Ps.109.6), which is where the 8 comes from. The pointed bytes separate them: an accent-stripped sweep of the actual 109:6 token יְמִינֽוֹ returns 4 verses (web:Ps.20.6 = oshb:Ps.20.7, oshb:Ps.78.54, web:Ps.89.25 = oshb:Ps.89.26, oshb:Ps.109.6). The other three read יָ֭מֵינוּ at oshb:Ps.90.9, יָ֭מֵינוּ at oshb:Ps.90.12, and יָמֵֽינוּ at oshb:Ps.90.14 -- 'our days', a different lexeme with an identical skeleton. This is the short-token homography the toolkit records for the two-letter divine-name case: skeleton parity, pointing differs, so a naive skeleton count is not evidence. Offered for the right-hand root, the 8 should be 4 verses.

challenges.claim: 'cohortative' at oshb:Ps.109.30 is a form label the staged evidence cannot carry, because the verb's class has no distinguishing cohortative morpheme.
challenges.evidence: The opening token is א֘וֹדֶ֤ה at oshb:Ps.109.30 (byte tier). The staged extract has no morphology layer, so the label must be argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses. The bytes give a III-he 1cs form, a class in which the cohortative carries no distinguishing final morpheme, so the token is formally identical to a plain 1cs imperfect; the skeleton sweeps to 8 verses book-wide (web:Ps.7.17 = oshb:Ps.7.18, web:Ps.9.1 = oshb:Ps.9.2, oshb:Ps.32.5, web:Ps.54.6 = oshb:Ps.54.8, oshb:Ps.109.30, oshb:Ps.111.1, oshb:Ps.118.19, oshb:Ps.138.2) with no formal variant among them to contrast against. WEB reads a plain future, “I will give great thanks to Yahweh with my mouth.” (web:Ps.109.30). The volitive sense may well be right; the morphological label is not derivable from what is staged, and the neighbouring signal in the same field states a form claim the source can support (the fronted independent pronouns at oshb:Ps.109.28).
